payload.text: URGENT · Powerful earthquake strikes southern Turkey · ISTANBUL (AP) — A powerful earthquake struck southern Turkey early Monday, shaking buildings across the region and sending people into the streets in freezing temperatures, officials said. The magnitude and the extent of the damage were not immediately clear.

The magnitude and the extent of the damage were not immediately clear.

payload.text: Rescuers dig by hand in Antakya · ANTAKYA, Turkey (AP) — Residents of Antakya dug through collapsed apartment blocks with their hands and kitchen tools on Monday morning as rescue teams struggled to reach the worst-hit neighbourhoods, local officials said.
payload.textEn: Rescuers dig by hand in Antakya · ANTAKYA, Turkey (AP) — Residents of Antakya dug through collapsed apartment blocks with their hands and kitchen tools on Monday morning as rescue teams struggled to reach the worst-hit neighbourhoods, local officials said.

payload.reason: URGENT · Bridge impassable in Antakya · ANTAKYA, Turkey (AP) — A bridge over the Asi River in central Antakya is impassable after the earthquake, provincial officials said Monday. Rescue and supply vehicles were being sent around the city centre.

payload.text: URGENT · Second powerful quake hits southern Turkey · ANTAKYA, Turkey (AP) — A second powerful earthquake of magnitude 7.5 struck southern Turkey on Monday afternoon, hours after the first, bringing down buildings that were already damaged and sending rescuers running from the rubble, witnesses said.

payload.text: Rescuers pull survivors from rubble in Hatay · ANTAKYA, Turkey (AP) — Rescue teams in Hatay province pulled several survivors from collapsed buildings on Monday, but officials said many more people remained trapped and heavy lifting equipment was in short supply.
payload.textEn: Rescuers pull survivors from rubble in Hatay · ANTAKYA, Turkey (AP) — Rescue teams in Hatay province pulled several survivors from collapsed buildings on Monday, but officials said many more people remained trapped and heavy lifting equipment was in short supply.

payload.text: Officials deny gas leak at Antakya tent camp · ANTAKYA, Turkey (AP) — Officials in Hatay province on Monday denied social media reports of a gas leak at a tent camp near the stadium in Antakya, saying utility crews had found no leak and no evacuation had been ordered.
payload.textEn: Officials deny gas leak at Antakya tent camp · ANTAKYA, Turkey (AP) — Officials in Hatay province on Monday denied social media reports of a gas leak at a tent camp near the stadium in Antakya, saying utility crews had found no leak and no evacuation had been ordered.

payload.text: Freezing night ahead for Turkey quake survivors · ANTAKYA, Turkey (AP) — Temperatures in Antakya were forecast to fall to minus 3 degrees Celsius overnight, and officials said tens of thousands of people were sleeping outdoors or in cars with little shelter.
payload.textEn: Freezing night ahead for Turkey quake survivors · ANTAKYA, Turkey (AP) — Temperatures in Antakya were forecast to fall to minus 3 degrees Celsius overnight, and officials said tens of thousands of people were sleeping outdoors or in cars with little shelter.

payload.text: Aid convoys head for Hatay as survivors face a second cold night · ANTAKYA, Turkey (AP) — Aid convoys were heading for Hatay province on Tuesday as survivors who spent the night outdoors queued for hot food, blankets and fuel, officials and residents said.
payload.textEn: Aid convoys head for Hatay as survivors face a second cold night · ANTAKYA, Turkey (AP) — Aid convoys were heading for Hatay province on Tuesday as survivors who spent the night outdoors queued for hot food, blankets and fuel, officials and residents said.

payload.reason: Antakya bridge reopens to light traffic · ANTAKYA, Turkey (AP) — A bridge over the Asi River in central Antakya reopened to pedestrians and light vehicles on Tuesday after engineers inspected it, provincial officials said.

payload.text: Hatay survivors endure a second day after twin quakes · ANTAKYA, Turkey (AP) — Thirty-six hours after the first earthquake, rescuers in Antakya were still pulling survivors from collapsed buildings, while tens of thousands of people sheltered in tents, schools and cars as temperatures stayed below freezing, officials said.
